faqs.q: Sec. 78-307. - Standards for repairs and restoration.
faqs.a:
(a)
Permittee responsibility.
The permittee shall be fully responsible for the cost and actual performance of all
               work in the public way. The permittee shall do all work in conformance with any and
               all engineering regulations, construction specifications, and design standards adopted
               by the city. These standards shall apply to all work in the public way unless otherwise
               indicated in the permit.
(b)
Restoration standards.
All restoration shall result in a work site condition equal to or better than that
               which existed prior to construction. In addition to the regulations, specifications,
               and standards referred to in subsection (a) of this section, the following provisions
               shall apply to work in the public rights-of-way of the city.
(1)
All trench and hole patches will be six inches in depth or equal to the existing asphalt
               depth if the existing asphalt is greater than six inches in depth.
(2)
All longitudinal trenches less than 50 feet in length and all transverse trenches
               shall be backfilled with cementatious flowable fill unless otherwise approved by the
               director. Nonexpansive, well-graded, granular material approved by the city will be
               acceptable for trench backfill of longitudinal trenches of length greater than 50
               feet.
(3)
The street in the area of the trench or hole shall be milled to a two-inch depth for
               a width of 12 feet, being centered along the length of the trench or hole. If the
               trench or hole width is greater than six feet, the milling width will be the maximum
               trench width plus six feet. The milling shall extend ten feet beyond both the beginning
               and the end of the trench or hole. The resulting milled surface shall be overlayed
               with a two-inch mat of asphalt in a manner to form a smooth and continuous street
               surface.
(4)
If a street, or overlay on that street, is less than five years old, the permittee
               shall complete this work within seven calendar days.
(5)
If a street, or most recent overlay of that street, is older than five years old,
               the permittee has the option of requesting to pay a degradation fee in lieu of performing
               the milling and overlay repair. The degradation fee shall be based upon the work required
               to maintain the street integrity and life span at its current level and prevent accelerated
               degradation of the street due to the penetration of the trench or hole. The degradation
               fee shall be calculated by staff and adopted annually by resolution and shall be based
               on the actual cost to the city of completing the work.
(6)
In all cases, the longitudinal limits of restoration will extend past the street cut
               by a minimum of ten feet in each direction.
(7)
Restoration work shall be completed within seven calendar days.
(8)
In all cases, the trench cut shall be paved and maintained as an all weather surface
               until such time as the permanent surface is installed.
(Code 1981, § 27-216; Ord. No. 3717, § 1, 8-27-2001)
